explanation: Genetic studies put fungi and animals on one branch of life. Like us, fungi cannot make their own food, and their cell walls contain chitin, the tough material of insect shells.

claims.text: Fungi, including mushrooms, are more closely related to animals than to plants.
Genetic studies place fungi and animals together in a single group, the opisthokonts, separate from plants.
Fungi cannot make their own food by photosynthesis.
Fungal cell walls contain chitin, which also forms the outer skeletons of insects.

evidence.restatement: Molecular phylogenies group fungi and animals in the opisthokonts, apart from plants.
Fungi do not photosynthesize; they absorb food from their surroundings.
Fungal cell walls contain chitin, the same polymer that forms much of an insect's exoskeleton.
Fungi and animals are sister groups, more closely related to each other than either is to plants.
Animals and fungi are placed together in the opisthokonts, separate from plants.
Fungal cell walls contain chitin, the material of insect exoskeletons.
